SFT is nice. Just the thing is you need to be really focused, attentive, and observant in his class to understand the topic. If you get distracted for even 1 minute, you'll be lost. But overall he's good. Plus point: if you don't understand what he says, go through the slides. You NEED to do SELF STUDY of course. If aren't into self-studying, he ain't for you.
(I have heard je uni learning er jonno bhalo na, but honestly, from prior experiences, I can say he's a thousand times better than many others.)
Pros:
1. His lectures are comprehensive and honestly pretty easy
2. He doesn't skip any topic from the syllabus. I have heard many faculties do. Ami in case kichu na bujhle amr oneek friend jara ei course ta amr aage kore felse ode jiggesh korle many time answer paisi je amder faculty oi topic ta skip korse
3. Sir has a very comprehensive lecture schedule, designed as per the student's need. He will start with "Set" (a topic we are familiar with) then gradually move to other topics and end with logic and number theory (topics we are less familiar with) whereas in most cases faculties start with logic. So yeah, it helps a lot.
3. If you can't understand any part, ask him, sir will explain it. If still have any troubles, go through the slides by yourself and you'll understand the topic.
4. Yes, he repeats questions or at least, makes them similar, so collect the previous year's questions and solve them.
5. If you want to make your basic strong, solve all the odd questions from the Exercise of the book.
6. Questions are easy.
7. Sir tries his best to teach you!!!!
8. Really easy going.
Not so sure about grading tho. (Update: He curves depending on the section)
